_comment: Does the pertinence classifier still separate a CONDITION from a REPORT? Every string here is judged by ETL/terms/classify_eligibility_pertinence.py alongside the live corpus, into the same digest-keyed cache, and web/scripts/check_gate_pertinence.ts asserts the cached verdict equals `expect`. A prompt edit, a model change or a temperature of enthusiasm that stops catching the sentence which caused all of this fails the build.
_why_not_a_word_list: The four `report` cases that came from the incident are all state-aid selectivity findings, so a checker built only from them would be an enumeration of one lexical family. The controls are chosen to break that: `decision_text_real_condition` is a sentence from the same kind of document, in the same register, that states a genuine condition and must stay `condition`; `budget_and_duration` is a `report` that has nothing to do with selectivity. The property is the KIND of statement, not the vocabulary of state aid.
_the_three_way_line: v2 split `report` into `report` and `demand_match` after the binary property judged 40 deciding gates `report` and only about five of them were the defect; the rest stated the size or the channel of the offer, which intake asks the founder to state their counterpart for. The three cases that pin the new line are `ticket_ceiling` and `financing_channel` (must be demand_match, or ~20 correct gates stop deciding) against `budget_and_duration` and `ipcei_hy2use_country_framing` (must stay report, or the carve-out becomes a loophole that readmits the original defect). Delete none of the four: each one is the other's guard rail.

cases.why: The sentence the 2026-08-07 retraction removed from eligibility_text and left encoded as a filter gate. A compatibility finding about aid already granted to a named beneficiary list; it can never be true-or-false OF AN APPLICANT.
cases.text: The Member States only grant support to the beneficiaries listed section 2.2.6 and the funding is not available to all undertakings in a comparable situation.

cases.why: The same finding as encoded in eligibility_gates.requirement, which is the form that reached verdict.ts::isFilter().
cases.text: Only the specific companies listed as Direct Participants (selected via national open and transparent calls) are eligible aid beneficiaries under the notified IPCEI Batteries measures.

cases.why: Same selectivity finding, different scheme and different wording -- the classifier must generalise past the exact sentence.
cases.text: Only pre-selected undertakings listed in the participating Member States' notification and forming part of the Hy2Infra individual projects are eligible aid beneficiaries.

cases.why: The worst of the four: it was llm_2pass and resolved onto entityCountries, so it could have decided a verdict against a founder in the wrong country. Naming six Member States does not make it a condition -- the beneficiaries were already chosen.
cases.text: Only the listed direct participants established in the six participating Member States (Slovakia, Hungary, France, Italy, Belgium, Spain) are eligible beneficiaries of the notified aid measures under the IPCEI Med4Cure.

cases.why: A REPORT with no selectivity language anywhere in it. True of the instrument, actionable by nobody. Present so the test does not degenerate into a selectivity detector -- and, since v2, doing double duty as the control on `demand_match`: this is a fact about MONEY, in euros, and still a report, because nobody is asked what overall budget they would prefer a scheme to have. The offer's shape is wantable; the scheme's administration is not.
cases.text: The scheme has an estimated overall budget of EUR 150 million and will run until 31 December 2027, with aid awarded in annual tranches by the managing authority.

cases.why: v3, AND A REAL REGRESSION THIS CAUGHT. Verbatim from a live Latvian gate. The v2 property judged it `condition`, reasoning that a reader 'can check whether they are a listed centre' -- which is true, and the answer is no, and it is no for every reader who will ever see it. It is the IPCEI defect wearing the grammar of a requirement: 'may only be submitted by' looks like a rule about applicants, and names eight companies. This case exists because the four IPCEI cases did NOT catch it: they are all state-aid decision prose about aid already granted, and this is a call page telling you who may apply. A condition must DISCRIMINATE -- be true of some readers and false of others. If this flips to `condition`, the classifier has stopped testing that and is back to testing grammar.
cases.text: Project applications may only be submitted by a closed, named list of eight competence centres (limited liability companies), such as 'LEO pētījumu centrs', the Latvian Food Competence Centre, the IT Competence Centre, the Forestry Sector Competence Centre, the Mechanical Engineering Competence Centre, the Pharmacy/Biomedicine/Medical Technology Competence Centre, ETKC, and VMKC.

cases.why: v2. Judged `report` by the binary property, and demoting it would have been wrong: `ticketBand` is a question we ask the founder, so this compares the offer against what they said they want. A founder seeking EUR 20m is genuinely not served by this loan. If it flips to `report`, roughly twenty ticket-size gates lose the ability to decide and the brief starts recommending instruments an order of magnitude too small.
cases.text: The maximum loan amount is EUR 250,000.

cases.why: v2. The same carve-out on a non-numeric axis: `borrowerModel` is an intake question, and this says the money reaches companies through funds rather than directly. An operating company should not be matched to a fund-of-funds vehicle, and this gate is the only thing that says so.
cases.text: Invest-NL invests as a limited partner / fund investor into venture capital funds rather than lending or granting directly to companies.

cases.why: THE TRAP THAT KEEPS demand_match HONEST, and a live gate: llm_2pass, resolved onto entityCountries, still deciding as of 2026-08-08. It names Member States, and `entityCountries` is something intake asks about -- so a classifier that reasoned 'mentions an intake field, therefore demand_match' would promote a selectivity finding straight back into a filter. It is a statement about aid already granted under 107(3)(b) to undertakings already participating. Mentioning a thing the founder is asked about is not the same as offering them something.
cases.text: Aid is granted by the notified Member States to participating undertakings located/operating in those Member States under Article 107(3)(b) TFEU as an IPCEI.

cases.why: Binds a beneficiary only AFTER an award, so nothing in it is a bar an applicant could clear before applying. A different failure shape from selectivity, and one that migration 013 measured at ~19% of the llm_cited tier.
cases.text: The beneficiary shall submit an annual implementation report to the granting authority within three months of the end of each financial year and shall retain all supporting documents for ten years.

cases.why: THE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL. Same document type, same legal register, same 'undertakings' vocabulary as the four findings above -- and it states a test an applicant can apply to themselves. A checker that fires on state-aid decision prose fails here.
cases.text: Aid may not be granted to undertakings in difficulty within the meaning of the Guidelines on State aid for rescuing and restructuring non-financial undertakings in difficulty, nor to undertakings subject to an outstanding recovery order.

cases.why: Narrow, exclusionary, and phrased as a restriction -- and still a condition, because a reader can check it against their own company. Narrowness is not the property; actionability is.
cases.text: Only undertakings active in the primary production of agricultural products and established in the region of Andalusia are eligible to apply.

cases.why: Guards the other direction: a condition stated as how the scheme has operated is still a condition. If this flips to `report`, the classifier has started demoting real rules for being written in the wrong tense, which would cost recall rather than protect founders.
cases.text: The programme has funded only projects with a total eligible cost above EUR 500 000, and applications below that threshold have not been considered.
